question:
An unknown porous material is brought to your laboratory. The material contains already some water, but clearly not all pores are filled.

The following measurements are taken:
1. Total mass of the sample as it was brought into the lab: $ 1523.6 \text{ g}$. Mass of the oven-dried sample: $1318.3\text{ g}$
3. Total volume of the sample: $728.2\text{ cm}^3$
4. Density of the matrix materials: $2.70 \text{ g/cm}^3$

Calculate the porosity $\phi$ to two decimal places
For the same sample, calculate the void ratio $e$ to two decimal places

Bonus question (helps for the rest of the course): For the same sample, calculate the volumetric water content $\theta$ to two decimal places

Yes, you will need to look up the definition of volumetric water content. You know... in a book or online.
What would be the mass of $1\text{m}^3$ of the unknown porous material if it was completely saturated? Answer in kg and two decimal places.
